question.text: Mr. Vikram Menon, an HNI, wants to invest in a newly launched Category II Private Equity AIF managed by Konark Capital. He is NOT an Accredited Investor, NOT an employee of the AIF, and the fund is NOT a Large Value Fund. What is the MINIMUM commitment he must make to participate?

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI (AIF) Regulations prescribe a minimum investment of INR 1 crore per investor in an AIF scheme. The INR 1 crore minimum is not applicable to Accredited Investors, and a separate INR 25 lakh carve-out applies to employees/directors of the AIF or Manager. The Angel Fund regime is also separate: no minimum value applies to investment in an Angel Fund by an angel investor (Angel Funds have a different per-investee-company investment range of INR 10 lakh to INR 25 crore). None of these carve-outs apply to Mr. Menon, so the INR 1 crore floor governs. The Trap: INR 25 lakh is the employees/directors carve-out, not the general investor floor. INR 50 lakh is the PMS investor minimum under a different product regime. INR 10 lakh is the lower end of the Angel Fund per-investee-company investment range, not an investor-level minimum for a Cat II PE scheme. Note: The carve-outs (Accredited Investor, employee/director, Angel Fund, Large Value Fund) each have specific eligibility conditions in the source; default to INR 1 crore unless a carve-out is clearly documented for the investor.
